atoms.text: This guide describes how to let the Querylane batch query service read Parquet files from the bucket sales-events-raw and write result sets back to the same bucket. The bucket and the IAM role QuerylaneExecutionRole both belong to account 111122223333. Because access does not cross an account boundary, the grant is made entirely through an identity-based policy attached to the role. Create a policy that allows ListBucket on the bucket and GetObject on the prefix events/parquet/. Add PutObject on the prefix query-results/ to the same policy so the service can write its output files. Attach the policy to QuerylaneExecutionRole and leave the bucket policy unchanged. Configure Querylane to assume this role when a query is submitted. Run a test query over one partition and confirm that a result object appears under query-results/. If the query fails with an access denied error, check the resource ARNs in the identity-based policy for typos in the bucket name or prefix.

This guide describes how to let the Querylane batch query service read Parquet files from the bucket sales-events-raw and write result sets back to the same bucket. The bucket belongs to account 444455556666, while the IAM role QuerylaneExecutionRole belongs to account 111122223333. Because access crosses an account boundary, the bucket owner must grant it through a bucket policy statement. In account 444455556666, add a statement naming the role ARN from account 111122223333 as the principal. The statement allows ListBucket on the bucket, GetObject on the prefix events/parquet/, and PutObject on the prefix query-results/. In account 111122223333, the role also needs an identity-based policy that allows the same actions on those resources. Configure Querylane to assume this role when a query is submitted. Run a test query over one partition and confirm that a result object appears under query-results/. If the query fails with an access denied error, check that the principal ARN in the bucket policy exactly matches the role ARN.

This guide covers granting the Streamweld ingestion service write access to the bucket clickstream-landing, where it stores compacted JSON-lines files every five minutes. The bucket and the role StreamweldWriterRole are both in account 222233334444. Since both resources share one account, access is granted only by the role's identity-based policy. Write a policy that allows PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on the prefix compacted/ in the bucket. Add ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket so the service can clean up incomplete uploads. Attach the policy to StreamweldWriterRole and do not edit the bucket policy. In the Streamweld pipeline settings, set the destination bucket to clickstream-landing and the output prefix to compacted/. Start the pipeline and verify that the first compacted file appears within one flush interval. If uploads fail, inspect the role's policy for a missing multipart upload action.

This guide covers granting the Streamweld ingestion service write access to the bucket clickstream-landing, where it stores compacted JSON-lines files every five minutes. The bucket is owned by account 555566667777, and the role StreamweldWriterRole is in account 222233334444. Since the role is in a different account, the bucket owner must add a bucket policy statement to grant access. The statement names the account ID 222233334444 as the principal and allows PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on the prefix compacted/. It also allows ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket so the service can clean up incomplete uploads. The role in account 222233334444 needs a matching identity-based policy with the same actions. In the Streamweld pipeline settings, set the destination bucket to clickstream-landing and the output prefix to compacted/. Start the pipeline and verify that the first compacted file appears within one flush interval. If uploads fail, inspect both policies for a missing multipart upload action.

This guide explains how to give the Pipefold ETL runner access to a bucket holding raw CSV exports and cleaned output. The bucket crm-exports and the role PipefoldJobRole are in account 333344445555. Access is granted solely through an identity-based policy on the role, and the bucket policy stays as it is. The policy allows GetObject on the prefix raw/ and ListBucket restricted to that prefix with a condition on the list prefix. It also allows PutObject on the prefix cleaned/, where Pipefold writes normalized Parquet files. Attach the policy to PipefoldJobRole. Register the role in the Pipefold job definition as the execution identity. Trigger a job on a sample file and confirm that a Parquet file with the same base name appears under cleaned/. If the job lists no files, confirm that the list-prefix condition matches the prefix the job requests.

This guide shows how to let the Logsift log analytics service read archived application logs and write daily summary reports. The log archive is the bucket app-logs-archive, and the role LogsiftReaderRole is in account 777788889999 along with the bucket. Because the account is the same, the grant lives only in the role's identity-based policy. Add GetObject and ListBucket for the prefix logs/year=2026/ so Logsift can scan the partitioned archive. Add PutObject for the prefix reports/daily/ to hold the generated summaries. Attach the policy to the role without modifying the bucket policy. Set the Logsift scan schedule to run at 02:00 UTC with the role as its execution identity. After the first run, check that a summary file named for the previous date exists under reports/daily/. If the scan reports zero objects, verify the partition prefix in the policy against the object keys.

This guide describes granting the Rollmark aggregation service access to hourly metric partitions and a table of rolled-up results. The bucket metrics-warehouse and the role RollmarkAggregatorRole are in account 121212121212. Access is provided only through the role's identity-based policy, and no bucket policy changes are made. The policy allows GetObject and ListBucket on the prefix hourly/ for reading input partitions. It allows PutObject and DeleteObject on the prefix rollups/daily/ so Rollmark can replace a day's output when it reruns. Attach the policy to RollmarkAggregatorRole. Configure the Rollmark schedule to assume that role for each daily aggregation. Run a backfill for one day and confirm that exactly one set of files exists under the matching rollups/daily/ date folder. If a rerun leaves stale files, check that the policy includes DeleteObject.

This guide explains how to give an analyst IAM user, mara.chen, access to run ad hoc Cohortly queries against event data. Cohortly reads Avro files from the bucket product-events and writes cohort tables to a results location. The user and the bucket are in account 454545454545. Since there is one account, the grant is made by an identity-based policy attached to the user's group, and the bucket policy is not touched. The policy allows GetObject and ListBucket on the prefix avro/events/. It allows PutObject on the prefix cohorts/mara.chen/ so each analyst's output stays separated. Add mara.chen to the group that carries the policy. Have the user submit a Cohortly query and verify that the output files land under cohorts/mara.chen/. If the output is rejected, confirm the user's name in the prefix of the resource path.

This guide covers configuring the Tallyport export service to read query inputs from one prefix and deliver CSV result files to another. Both prefixes are in the bucket finance-ledger-data, which is in account 676767676767 with the role TallyportExportRole. The grant is carried only by the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policyremains unmodified. The policy allows GetObject on the prefix ledger/closed/ and ListBucket on the bucket for that prefix. It allows PutObject on the prefix exports/csv/, with a condition requiring the object to be written with server-side encryption. Attach the policy to TallyportExportRole. Select the role in the Tallyport export profile and enable server-side encryption on the write path. Run an export for a single closed period and confirm that a CSV file appears under exports/csv/. If writes are denied, check that the request includes the encryption header the condition requires.

This guide describes how to let the Schemaward validation service read newly arrived data files and write rejected-record reports. Incoming files are placed under the prefix inbox/ in the bucket partner-feeds, and Schemaward runs under the role SchemawardValidatorRole. The bucket and the role are both in account 232323232323, so the grant is made only through the role's identity-based policy. The policy allows GetObject, ListBucket, and DeleteObject on the prefix inbox/, because validated files are removed after processing. It also allows PutObject on the prefix rejects/ for the JSON reports of records that fail schema checks. Attach the policy to the role and leave the bucket policy unchanged. Point Schemaward at the inbox/ prefix and set the role as its runtime identity. Upload a file with one malformed row and confirm that a report appears under rejects/ and the source file is removed from inbox/. If the source file remains, check that DeleteObject is present in the policy.
